Aisha —

Thanks for taking this on. We’re in the middle of an internal compliance audit and need a quick architecture snapshot of the Private VPC you’ll be deploying for Acme Financial. Primary asks from our security team: control-plane/data-plane demarcation, egress proofing (where traffic leaves the colo/VPC), and an ops runbook for incident handoff (who we contact, what escalation levels look like).

We have a window next week for a short review (30 min). Can you share the current reference diagram and any runbook deltas you anticipate for our environment? If it helps, I can share the Acme security checklist ahead of time.

Appreciate it —
Tom Keene

Date: 2026-08-17T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private VPC architecture snapshot and audit ask — reference artifacts attached

Tom / Lara —

Attaching the artifacts Aisha mentioned:
- vpc-reference-diagram-v3.pdf (high-level: control-plane management plane on isolated subnet, data-plane in tenant pods, explicit egress NAT and proxy choke points labeled)
- egress-proof-checklist.xlsx (checks we perform for outbound firewall/NAT rules, required Flow Logs and where they land, and suggested retention for audit purposes)
- runbook-deltas.md (customer-specific steps for Acme: IP allowlist process, KMS key rotation window, emergency egress override)

Summary notes (short):
- Control plane: managed control plane components (api-server, job-scheduler, rollout controller) run in a hardened management VPC-subnet with restricted inbound. All API access goes through mTLS and RBAC gating.
- Data plane: tenant inference nodes run in separate subnets with egress through a NAT/proxy stack in the shared services zone. KV cache and model artifacts are served via signed requests from an internal object store; no direct outbound to internet except through proxy.
- Egress proofing: we place an egress choke at the shared services NAT/proxy and mirror Flow Logs to the audit log collector for 90 days. We can extend to 365 days if required (will impact storage costs).

Open items for the call:
1) Confirm who at Acme needs KMS/HSM audit access (read-only vs key-admin).
2) Decide retention target for flow logs (90 vs 365 days).
3) Confirm whether Acme requires an on-prem proxy appliance vs cloud-hosted egress proxy.

Attachments: vpc-reference-diagram-v3.pdf (application/pdf), egress-proof-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), runbook-deltas.md (text/markdown)

On Tue we’ll walk through the diagram and mark any changes live.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — the artifacts look good and this addresses most of the audit asks. Two quick clarifications from the Acme security team before the review:

1) Can you add a short appendix in runbook-deltas.md that describes the step-by-step process for an emergency egress override (who signs, what checks are skipped, how we revert). They want a retention/authorization chain recorded for audits.
2) For the flow logs retention: Acme prefers 365 days. Please include an estimated storage delta and monthly cost in the checklist if possible.

If you can send an updated runbook-deltas.md with those two items before Tue 10:00 PDT, we’ll be ready to sign off during the review. Otherwise we can record those items as conditional actions.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Tom
